A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VD3D, with matching authors, central contributions and retained results. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original camera-control experiments, a user study, ablations, and appendix results for multiview reconstruction and video-generation metrics.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, conditioning ablations, synthetic-trajectory evaluations and experiments with a vanilla DiT backbone.

M1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds a latent-video DiT implementation using the CogVideoX autoencoder, applying ControlNet conditioning to ordinary token attention instead of FIT read attention. This substantially extends the implemented architecture. The reported FIT conditioning branch also drops the input zero convolution present in v1, retaining the output residual convolution.

E1.justification: RealEstate10K, MSR-VTT and the existing video/multiview tasks remain. Appendix B.4 adds quantitative coverage of synthetic rotation-only trajectories and specified paths with substantial directional changes, extending the camera-input scenarios beyond v1's quantitative evaluation on dataset trajectories.

E2.justification: v3 adds original U-Net versions of MotionCtrl and CameraCtrl to Tables 2-4, plus MotionCtrl (latents) and CameraCtrl (patches) adaptations in Tables 5-7. These substantially broaden the comparisons beyond v1's selected transformer adaptations. MotionCtrl (frozen) is retained in the appendix, not removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include rotation trajectories sampled across axes and angular extents of 0-120 degrees, and 11 specified trajectories evaluated with 1000 prompts. Appendix B.5 introduces an 11.5B DiT configuration with separately documented training and rectified-flow inference. The original FIT training budget, user-study design and established metrics remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds ablations testing camera matrices and Plücker embeddings through the context vector, alternative baseline injection locations, and synthetic-trajectory generalization tests. The vanilla DiT experiment also tests transfer beyond FIT. These substantially expand the evidence about conditioning design and generality; the original three ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same chi-square significance testing for the user study. Neither adds confidence intervals, seed-based variability summaries or other uncertainty procedures. The approximately 150 development training runs were already disclosed in v1.

E6.justification: All 26 original numerical result rows are retained, including relocated frozen-baseline results. v3 substantially expands the results with new comparators, ablations, trajectory tests and DiT experiments. For example, Table 10 reports DiT MSR-VTT translation/rotation errors of 0.486/0.047; these are results under a different backbone, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The formal conditioning mapping changes from Conv_pluck(c) in v1 Eqs. (4)-(5) to c+v in v3 Eq. (4), without the input convolution. Explicit video-token fusion also resolves an omission relative to v1 Fig. 3, which already depicted fusion. The diffusion loss and camera geometry remain equivalent, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: first camera control for joint spatiotemporal video transformers, ControlNet-like Plücker conditioning, and state-of-the-art controllability and quality. The additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 removes the speculative explanation that CameraCtrl needs longer training because of random initialization. Appendix B.2 adds a distribution-based interpretation of FID/FVD degradation and proposes joint training; B.5 argues applicability beyond FIT. Existing limitations concerning dynamic consistency, frozen upsampling and short SnapVideo outputs remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds substantial DiT architecture, training and inference specifications, identifies the two-layer GELU camera MLP and 230M trainable parameters, and states that FIT-block source code accompanies the paper. Original FIT optimizer and hardware details move to Appendix C. The earlier user-study compensation amount is no longer disclosed.

R1.justification: Appendix A introduces extensive coverage of static 3D generation and reconstruction, including score distillation, multiview generation and feed-forward reconstruction. v3 also explicitly distinguishes PixArt-delta's spatial conditioning from its spatiotemporal camera conditioning and adds earlier Plücker-related work. Much of the existing 4D discussion is relocated rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: Most central prose and the main scientific narrative remain closely matched. v3 makes local clarifications, moves detailed training and extended related work into appendices, adds standalone ethics and reproducibility statements, and changes citation style. These are limited editorial and organizational revisions rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redrawn with clearer token paths and component labels. Tables 2-4 expand, and Tables 5-11 add extensive displays, including relocated frozen-baseline rows. Other qualitative figures largely retain their examples with caption and formatting changes, while the ICLR template changes typography and placement throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's FIT-based adaptations and dataset-derived quantitative trajectories. Original U-Net comparisons, alternative conditioning implementations, constructed-trajectory tests and vanilla DiT experiments address important gaps in comparison coverage and architectural generality. Added implementation documentation improves reproducibility. The gains come from stronger supporting evidence and clearer specification, while original scores remain unchanged; uncertainty reporting remains limited.
